Use an HTTP middleware. To create a middleware you use the decorator `@app.middleware("http")` on top of a function.[1] The function receives the request and a function `call_next` that will receive the `request` as a parameter.[1] You can then further modify the `response` before returning it.[1]

The docs show exactly this case: you could add a custom header `X-Process-Time` containing the time in seconds that it took to process the request and generate a response[2]:

```python
import time

from fastapi import FastAPI, Request

app = FastAPI()


@app.middleware("http")
async def add_process_time_header(request: Request, call_next):
    start_time = time.perf_counter()
    response = await call_next(request)
    process_time = time.perf_counter() - start_time
    response.headers["X-Process-Time"] = str(process_time)
    return response
```

The example uses `time.perf_counter()` instead of `time.time()` because it can be more precise for these use cases.[2]

If browser clients need to read this header, you need to add them to your CORS configurations ([CORS (Cross-Origin Resource Sharing)](cors.md)) using the parameter `expose_headers`[1].

Source: https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/tutorial/middleware/
